triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix eligibility test was only `eitc_child_count > 0 or count_where(member_of_tax_unit, eitc_childless_age_eligible) > 0` plus two opaque inputs, so it omitted 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(I) and (III) (US principal abode for more than half the year, not a dependent of another taxpayer), 32(c)(1)(B) (taxpayer who is another taxpayer's qualifying child), 32(c)(1)(C) (section 911 claimants), 32(c)(1)(D) (nonresident aliens absent a 6013(g)/(h) election), 32(e) (short taxable year), 32(k) (fraud/reckless-disregard disallowance periods and prior deficiency denials), and 32(m)'s SSN definition, and it counted any tax-unit member — including dependents — toward the childless age test rather than the taxpayer or spouse.
triage.triage_notes: Provision not separately resolved; the added proof-atom `text:` fields carry the corpus excerpts and the module summary is verbatim statutory text. Two secondary formula corrections worth noting: `eitc_maximum` moved from the Rev. Proc. published maximum-credit table to 32(a)(2)(A)'s 'credit percentage of the earned income amount' (phase_in_rate * earned_income_amount), and `eitc_phased_in` moved from `min(eitc_maximum, earned_income * rate)` to 32(a)(1)'s `rate * min(earned_income, earned_income_amount)` — numerically these differ only by the Rev. Proc. rounding of the published maximum. `eitc_before_eligibility` changed from `min(P, max(0, M-R))` to `max(0, min(P, M-R))`, which is algebraically identical for non-negative P. The qualifying-child test gained the 32(c)(3)(C) US-abode requirement and the 32(c)(3)(B) married-child exception. The 32(b)(1) percentage tables and the childless age bounds (25/65) are unchanged. The `us:policies/irs/rev-proc-2025-32/earned-income-credit` import is retained for the (b)(2)/(i)(1) indexed amounts.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as provenance-only or as new scope the module never claimed, and both fail: `rules[eitc_demographic_eligible].versions[0].formula` itself changed from a two-term test (`eitc_child_count > 0 or count_where(member_of_tax_unit, eitc_childless_age_eligible) > 0`) to a conjunction that adds the US-abode test, the not-a-dependent test, the qualifying-child-of-another-taxpayer bar, the section 911 exception, the nonresident-alien bar, the joint-return rule, the full-12-month rule, and the 32(k) disallowance bars. The pinned corpus text (us-rulespec-2026-07-13, body sha256 f829a778…) shows those conditions verbatim in 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(I) and (III), (B), (C), (D), and the pre-fix rule cited `26 USC 32(c)(1)(A)` while `eitc_eligible` cited `32(c), 32(d), 32(i)`, so the omitted conditions sat inside the scope the module already claimed — this is a missing-clause correction, not added coverage. The added proof-atom excerpt the first reader quoted is backed by a real formula term (`and not taxpayer_claims_section_911_benefits`), so the excerpt-only/mechanical escape does not apply. Kind stands: the fix predominantly adds conditions the source states and the encoding lacked.

triage.verifier_notes: Competing kinds I considered and rejected as the primary label, but a reviewer should know they co-occur in the same rule rewrite: (1) wrong_entity_or_scope — the pre-fix childless branch tested ANY tax-unit member (`count_where(member_of_tax_unit, eitc_childless_age_eligible) > 0`) whereas 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(II) scopes the age test to the individual or, if married, the individual or spouse; the fix narrows to `childless_taxpayer_or_spouse_age_eligible_for_eitc`. (2) polarity_or_logic — the pre-fix married gate `(filing_status != 2 or satisfies_eitc_separated_spouse_rules)` in `eitc_eligible` fails open for married filers in any status coded other than 2, versus 32(d)(1)'s joint-return requirement; the fix is `(filing_status == 1 or not taxpayer_is_married_under_section_7703_a or satisfies_eitc_separated_spouse_rules)`. (3) untraceable_branch — `eitc_maximum` moved off the imported Rev. Proc. `eitc_maximum_credit_amounts[...]` table onto the statutory `eitc_phase_in_rate * eitc_earned_income_amount`; that is a re-grounding but arithmetically equivalent, so it carries little independent weight. Caveats: the 32(e) short-year and 32(k) disallowance/prior-deficiency terms are arguably scope the module never claimed (no pre-fix rule cited them), so if a reviewer wants the narrowest defect it is 32(c)(1)(A)(ii)(I)/(III), (B), (C), (D) — all squarely inside the rule's own cited source. Also note every new condition is an undefined opaque input (`taxpayer_claims_section_911_benefits`, `taxpayer_is_nonresident_alien_for_any_portion_of_year`, etc.), so the runtime effect depends on the caller supplying them; the first reader's "two opaque inputs" characterization of the pre-fix state is imprecise (pre-fix also leaned on `is_qualifying_child_dependent`, `filer_meets_eitc_identification_requirements`, `satisfies_eitc_separated_spouse_rules`). The commit is a wholesale regeneration of 12 modules with no per-module message, so the anchor evidence is the diff, not the commit text; the PR (#25, "Encode 26 USC 63(c) standard deduction") says nothing about section 32. Sibling rule `eitc_qualifying_child` shows the same unrepresented_clause pattern (adds 32(c)(3)(B) married exception, 32(c)(3)(C) US abode, 32(c)(3)(D) name/age/TIN), which corroborates the kind.
